articles.headline: One Iron Infusion Unlocks Hidden Exercise Power
articles.body: A randomized trial just showed that a single intravenous iron infusion significantly improved exercise capacity in people with heart failure and iron deficiency. The study tracked 65 patients over 12 weeks, measuring changes in VO2 max and walking distance. Those who received the infusion saw peak oxygen consumption jump about 10 percent compared to placebo, plus improvements in their ability to walk and their functional class. Iron is essential for both oxygen transport to muscles and mitochondrial energy production. This matters for anyone whose performance has mysteriously stalled despite solid training.
articles.takeaway: If you're struggling with exercise tolerance despite training hard, low iron might be the culprit. Worth testing.

articles.topic: Daily GLP-1 pill cuts sleep apnea in half
articles.headline: One Pill Cuts Your Sleep Apnea Burden by 50 Percent
articles.body: In two year-long trials published in JAMA, adults with moderate-to-severe sleep apnea and excess weight who took oral orforglipron had about 18 fewer breathing interruptions per hour after 52 weeks, compared to just 5 fewer in the placebo group. The drug also cut oxygen-deprivation episodes during sleep by over half and reduced inflammation markers. Importantly, it worked whether people were using PAP therapy or not. More than 40 percent of treated participants achieved at least a 50 percent reduction in their apnea-hypopnea index. This could be a game-changer for people who can't tolerate or don't respond well to traditional sleep apnea treatments.
articles.takeaway: If you've been struggling with sleep apnea despite other treatments, this deserves a conversation with your doctor.

articles.headline: How You Feel About Your Workout Predicts If You'll Stick With It
articles.body: A Finnish study of 299 adults found that emotional responses to exercise, not willpower or discipline, determine whether people actually stay consistent with fitness. People who felt pride, pleasure, and attraction to their workouts stuck with them long-term. Those with higher BMI reported less enjoyment and more extrinsic motives like appearance-based goals. The research suggests that the emotional quality of the experience itself matters more than initial motivation. Social support and non-judgmental environments were crucial for reducing negative feelings, especially for people who had uncomfortable gym experiences before.
articles.takeaway: Stop forcing workouts you hate. Find movement that feels good, and consistency will follow.

articles.headline: Swapping Your Salt Could Prevent Millions of Deaths
articles.body: A global modeling study across 193 countries found that switching from regular salt to potassium-enriched salt could prevent nearly three million deaths annually from cardiovascular and kidney disease. Just using potassium salt at home could prevent 1.85 million deaths and 6.19 million disease cases per year. Even partial transitions delivered substantial gains. The researchers modeled multiple scenarios including switching household salt, salt in processed foods, and salt in restaurant dishes. For people with diagnosed hypertension, the impact was even greater. This simple swap addresses a major driver of high blood pressure without requiring expensive medical interventions.
articles.takeaway: Your salt choice matters. Switching to potassium-enriched salt is one of the easiest heart-protective changes you can make.
articles.source: Nature Health / George Institute for Global Health

workout.title: Deadlift Strength Block: Heavy 4s + Front Squat & Leg Press Accessory
workout.tip: On each deadlift rep, take a full breath into your belly before the pull, brace as if bracing for a punch, and think 'push the floor away' rather than 'pull the bar up' — this cue keeps your back flat and hips loaded.
workout.warmup: 12 min: 3 min light bike or brisk walk to elevate heart rate → 10 hip circles each direction → 10 glute bridges → 10 bodyweight Romanian deadlifts → 8 goblet squats (light) → 2 sets deadlift warm-up: 8 reps at 40% 1RM, then 5 reps at 60% 1RM, then 3 reps at 72% 1RM

exercises.name: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.notes: Rest 3–4 min between sets. Set up with bar over mid-foot, grip just outside shins, hips hinge back until tension fills the hamstrings before the pull initiates. Each rep should be reset from the floor — no touch-and-go. Lower the bar with control, do not collapse the back on descent.

exercises.name: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.notes: Rest 2–3 min. Use a clean grip or cross-arm grip — elbows high is non-negotiable to keep the torso upright. Descend to parallel or below, keeping knees tracking over toes. This strengthens your quad drive and upper-back brace, which carries over directly to your deadlift lockout.

exercises.name: Leg Press
exercises.notes: Rest 90 sec. Feet shoulder-width, mid-platform. Lower the sled until hips begin to tuck — that is your depth cue. Press through the full foot, not just the toes. This is hypertrophy-adjacent accessory work — control the eccentric for 2–3 seconds on every rep.

workout.cooldown: 8 min: 60 sec standing quad stretch each leg → 60 sec kneeling hip flexor stretch each side → 60 sec supine piriformis figure-4 stretch each side → 60 sec child's pose with arms extended → 30 sec seated hamstring reach each leg
workout.description: This session anchors a strength phase with heavy barbell deadlifts at 85% 1RM across 4 sets of 4 reps, targeting maximal force production and posterior chain development. Front squats and leg press follow as accessory work to reinforce quad strength and positional integrity under load. Expect significant neural demand — this is a high-effort day requiring full recovery between sets.

meal.title: Cornbread & Blackstrap Molasses Spread
meal.description: A slice of tender cornbread with a spread of softened butter mixed with blackstrap molasses delivers fast carbs plus iron and B vitamins for aerobic endurance work. The slight sweetness and dense texture make it ideal for a 30-minute pre-run window.
meal.instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F and lightly grease a small cast-iron skillet or 6-inch cake pan.
2. Mix cornmeal, flour, and baking soda in a bowl.
3. Whisk together buttermilk, melted butter, and molasses; fold into dry ingredients until just combined.
4. Pour batter into skillet and bake 18–20 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
5. Cool slightly, then slice and spread with softened butter mixed with 1/2 tsp molasses.
meal.tip: Bake a batch of cornbread on Sunday and store in an airtight container. Toast a slice 30 minutes before your run for a warm, familiar pre-workout fuel that won't cause gut distress.
